title: filefacts-allowlist
description: The named file paths whose version metadata may be read for one application: an exact directory root plus one fixed file name, or an exact file. A server administrator sets it for the fleet, a client, a site or a cabinet through the device-settings route, with step-up and an audit entry; a Tier 1 or Tier 2 account, and a cabinet agent, never submits a path. entries null removes that level's list so the level above applies.

level.description: The level the list is set for. The most specific level with a list wins for a cabinet.

id.description: The client, site or cabinet id; null for the fleet (level fleet).

entries.description: At most 32 named paths, each with its own root. An empty list means "read nothing at this level", which still overrides the level above.

stepUpToken.description: A one-time step-up token bound to this exact action, level and these exact entries.

entry.description: One named file: the directory it lives in and its own file name. The server canonicalizes both and refuses to resolve anything else.

includeSha256.description: Also read the file's SHA-256. Off unless asked for: hashing reads the whole file, while a version resource is read from the file's header.

maxBytes.description: The largest file this entry may read, lower than the platform's own cap and never higher.

itemKey.description: The baseline item key this file stands for, in the applications category (app:<name>), so a version that differs from the site's baseline can be reported. No separators, no control characters.

directoryRoot.description: An absolute local directory on the cabinet with a drive letter, no relative segments, no trailing dot or space, no trailing separator, no alternate data stream, and no UNC, device or wildcard form.

fileName.description: One file name inside that root: a single name, no path separator, no alternate data stream, no wildcard, not a dot name, and no trailing dot or space.
